fullPassage:
(A) Ms. Blake walked along the edge of the soccer field, watching Eva pack up her things after practice. She paused for a moment, then called out, "Hey, Eva! How about staying a little longer? We can work on some drills — just the two of us." Eva hesitated. "I don't know, Coach. I'm pretty tired." Ms. Blake gave her a warm smile. "Just ten minutes. It'll be fun. I promise." Finally, Eva agreed, though she still seemed reluctant. They practiced passing the ball together.

(B) The next game, Ms. Blake watched from the sidelines as Eva played. There was a new confidence that hadn't been there before. Eva didn't score but led the team successfully. After the game she ran over, saying, "Thanks for believing in me, Coach." Ms. Blake smiled back. "You've always had it in you. I'm just here to remind you of that." Eva's face softened, as she realized she had been too hard on herself. She said to herself, "What matters is doing my best, not being perfect."

(C) Ms. Blake stepped closer and placed a reassuring hand on Eva's shoulder. She suggested, "You don't have to be perfect. Soccer isn't about perfection — it's about passion. And you've always had plenty of that." Eva's gaze met Ms. Blake's. "Do you really think so?" Ms. Blake said firmly, "Yes. The way you play, the energy you bring — that's what makes you special. Not the goals scored or the trophies won. It's the love you have for the game." Eva nodded thoughtfully.

(D) Ms. Blake noticed that Eva's movements were slow and that her focus seemed elsewhere. Breaking the silence, Ms. Blake asked, "Do you remember the final game last year?" "Yeah, I remember." Eva recalled the game where she scored three goals. "I was quite good back then." "You still are," replied Ms. Blake. "Well, now I'm so worried I can't score a goal or even pass the ball properly. I'm afraid of making mistakes," said Eva.

questions.passage: Ms. Blake walked along the edge of the soccer field, ①<u>watched</u> Eva pack up her things after practice. She paused for a moment. Eva hesitated. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: Eva가 짐을 싸는 것을 보면서(watching). ① watched → watching: 동시동작 분사구문.
det.analysis:
❌ ① watched → watching: walked와 동시에 일어나는 동작. 분사구문(현재분사).
✅ ② smile: 명사. 적절.
❌ ③ reluctant: 형용사(seemed의 보어). 적절.
❌ ④ passing: practiced + V-ing. 적절.
det.tip: 분사구문(동시동작): V-ing ~. watching = ~하면서 보다. practice + V-ing

questions.passage: Ms. Blake noticed that Eva's movements ①<u>were</u> slow. ②<u>Breaking</u> the silence, she asked about last year's final game. Eva recalled the game ③<u>which</u> she scored three goals. Eva was afraid of ④<u>making</u> mistakes.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 세 골을 넣은 경기를(where). ③ which → where: the game은 장소의 선행사. 관계부사 where.
det.analysis:
❌ ③ which → where: 'the game where she scored'. game은 장소적 개념. which를 쓰려면 in which.
✅ ① were: 복수 주어(movements). 적절.
❌ ② Breaking: 분사구문. 적절.
❌ ④ making: be afraid of + V-ing. 적절.
det.tip: 관계부사 where: 장소 선행사(game, place). which를 쓰려면 전치사 필요(in which)

questions.passage: Ms. Blake stepped closer and placed a reassuring hand on Eva's shoulder. Eva's gaze ①<u>met</u> Ms. Blake's. "The way you play, the energy you bring — that's ②<u>what</u> makes you special. Not the goals ③<u>scoring</u> or the trophies won." Eva's face softened, as she realized she had been too hard on ④<u>herself</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 넣은 골(scored)이나 획득한 트로피가 아니다. ③ scoring → scored: 골은 '넣어진' 것이므로 과거분사(수동).
det.analysis:
✅ ① met: 과거 동사. 적절.
❌ ③ scoring → scored: goals가 score 되는 것(수동). 'the goals scored'와 'the trophies won'이 병렬.
❌ ② what: 선행사 포함 관계대명사. 적절.
❌ ④ herself: 재귀대명사(Eva = she). 적절.
det.tip: 과거분사(수동): goals scored(넣어진 골), trophies won(획득한 트로피). 병렬 구조

questions.passage: Eva ①<u>hesitated</u>. "I'm pretty tired." Ms. Blake gave her a warm ②<u>smile</u>. Finally, Eva agreed, though she seemed reluctant. Ms. Blake noticed Eva's movements were slow. Eva recalled scoring three goals. "You still are," replied Ms. Blake. "Well, now I'm so ③<u>relaxed</u> I can't score or pass properly. I'm afraid of making mistakes." Ms. Blake said firmly that Eva's energy makes her ④<u>special</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: Eva는 걱정이 돼서(worried) 득점하거나 패스할 수 없었다. ③ relaxed(편안한)는 worried의 반의어로 부적절.
det.analysis:
❌ ③ relaxed → worried: 원문은 'I'm so worried'. relaxed는 반대.
✅ ① hesitated: 원문 그대로.
❌ ② smile: 원문 그대로.
❌ ④ special: 원문 그대로.
det.tip: worried(걱정하는)↔relaxed(편안한). be worried about = ~에 대해 걱정하다

questions.passage: Ms. Blake stepped closer and placed a ①<u>reassuring</u> hand on Eva's shoulder. "Soccer isn't about perfection — it's about passion." Eva nodded ②<u>thoughtfully</u>. The next game, there was a new ③<u>confidence</u> in Eva. She led the team successfully. Eva's face softened as she realized she had been too ④<u>easy</u> on herself.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 자신에게 너무 엄격했다(hard). ④ easy(쉬운/관대한)는 hard의 반의어로 부적절.
det.analysis:
❌ ④ easy → hard: 원문은 'too hard on herself'. easy는 반대.
✅ ① reassuring: 원문 그대로.
❌ ② thoughtfully: 원문 그대로.
❌ ③ confidence: 원문 그대로.
det.tip: hard on oneself(엄격한)↔easy on oneself(관대한). be too hard on = 너무 엄격하게 대하다

questions.passage: Ms. Blake noticed Eva's slow movements and distracted focus. She asked about last year's game. Eva remembered scoring three goals but said she was now afraid of mistakes. Ms. Blake told her soccer is about passion, not __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 축구는 열정에 관한 것이지, 완벽함(perfection)이 아니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① perfection: 원문 'Soccer isn't about perfection — it's about passion'.
❌ ② passion: 이것이 축구의 본질이라고 함. 빈칸은 반대.
❌ ③ teamwork: 언급 없음.
❌ ④ competition: 언급 없음.
det.tip: not A but B = A가 아니라 B. perfection(완벽)↔passion(열정)

questions.passage: Eva was reluctant to practice more. Her movements were slow and she feared making mistakes. After Ms. Blake's reassuring talk about passion over perfection, Eva showed new confidence in the next game. She realized the key lesson: __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: Winning is the only thing that matters in sports
Doing one's best is more important than being flawless
Talent alone determines an athlete's success

det.korean: 핵심 교훈: 최선을 다하는 것이 완벽한 것보다 중요하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ 원문 'What matters is doing my best, not being perfect'의 패러프레이징.
❌ ① 완벽한 연습: 글의 메시지와 반대.
❌ ② 이기는 것만 중요: 글에서 부정.
❌ ④ 재능만: 글의 주제가 아님.
det.tip: flawless = perfect. doing one's best = 최선을 다하는 것

questions.passage: Ms. Blake walked along the edge of the soccer field, watching Eva pack up her things after practice. She called out and asked Eva to stay longer for drills. Eva hesitated but eventually agreed.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: Eva가 Ms. Blake에게 추가 훈련을 먼저 요청했다.
Ms. Blake가 연습 후 Eva에게 추가 훈련을 제안했다.

det.korean: Ms. Blake가 연습 후 추가 훈련을 제안했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① 원문 'after practice' + 'How about staying a little longer?'와 일치.
❌ ② Ms. Blake가 먼저 제안.
❌ ③ 망설인 후 동의.
❌ ④ 연습 후.
det.tip: How about ~ing? = ~하는 것은 어때? (제안). after practice = 연습 후

questions.passage: Ms. Blake said, "Soccer isn't about perfection — it's about passion. The way you play, the energy you bring — that's what makes you special. Not the goals scored or the trophies won."
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
ch: Eva의 플레이 방식과 에너지가 그녀를 특별하게 만든다.
골이나 트로피가 Eva를 특별하게 만드는 것은 아니다.
Ms. Blake는 골을 넣는 것이 가장 중요하다고 말했다.
축구는 완벽함이 아니라 열정에 관한 것이다.

det.korean: Ms. Blake는 골이 아닌 열정이 중요하다고 했다. ④는 반대.
det.analysis:
❌ ④ 불일치: 원문은 'Not the goals scored'로 골 자체가 중요하지 않다고 함.
✅ ① 일치: it's about passion.
❌ ② 일치: that's what makes you special.
❌ ③ 일치: Not the goals scored or trophies won.
det.tip: Not A but B = A가 아니라 B. 원문 방향성 파악 필수

questions.passage: The next game, Eva showed new confidence. She didn't score but led the team successfully. After the game she said, "Thanks for believing in me, Coach." Ms. Blake replied, "You've always had it in you."
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
ch: 다음 경기에서 Eva에게 새로운 자신감이 있었다.
Ms. Blake는 Eva에게 그 능력이 항상 있었다고 말했다.

det.korean: Eva는 득점하지 못했다(didn't score). ③ '결정적인 골'은 반대.
det.analysis:
❌ ③ 불일치: didn't score. 골을 넣었다는 것은 틀림.
✅ ① 일치: new confidence.
❌ ② 일치: Thanks for believing in me.
❌ ④ 일치: You've always had it in you.
det.tip: didn't score but led = 득점은 없었지만 이끌었다

questions.passage: Eva was afraid of mistakes. Her coach told her soccer is about passion, not perfection. Eva regained confidence and led the team. She realized doing her best matters more than being perfect.

ch: How to Score More Goals in Soccer
The Importance of Winning Every Game
Passion Over Perfection: A Coach's Lesson
Why Athletes Should Never Make Mistakes

det.korean: 제목: 완벽보다 열정: 코치의 교훈.
det.analysis:
✅ ② 글의 핵심: 완벽주의 극복, 열정의 가치.
❌ ① 골 넣기 기술이 아님.
❌ ③ 이기는 것이 핵심이 아님.
❌ ④ 실수하지 않는 것이 아님.
det.tip: Passion Over Perfection = 완벽보다 열정. 글의 핵심 메시지를 제목으로

questions.passage: Eva feared mistakes and lost confidence. Ms. Blake encouraged her, emphasizing passion over perfection. Eva showed new confidence in the next game and realized doing her best is what truly matters.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 스포츠에서 경쟁이 선수 성장에 미치는 영향
코치가 선수에게 기술을 가르치는 효과적인 방법
완벽주의를 극복하고 최선을 다하는 태도의 중요성

det.korean: 주제: 완벽주의를 극복하고 최선을 다하는 태도의 중요성.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ Eva가 완벽주의 극복 → 최선의 가치 깨달음. 핵심.
❌ ① 경쟁이 아닌 내면의 변화.
❌ ② 기술 가르치기가 아닌 마인드셋.
❌ ③ 승리 추구가 아닌 완벽주의.
det.tip: 주제 = 글의 교훈. perfection(완벽) → passion/best effort(열정/최선)

questions.passage: "<u>You've always had it in you.</u> I'm just here to remind you of that."
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 <u>You've always had it in you</u>가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: Eva의 능력과 잠재력은 처음부터 있었다는 것

det.analysis:
✅ ② 'have it in you' = 내면에 능력이 있다. 코치는 상기시켜줄 뿐.
❌ ① 경기 승리와 다름.
❌ ③ 골 자체가 아닌 내면의 자질.
❌ ④ 코치의 역할을 부정하는 것이 아님.
det.tip: have it in you = 내면에 그 능력이 있다. remind = 상기시키다

questions.passage: Ms. Blake walked along the edge of the soccer field, watching Eva pack up her things after practice. <u>She</u> paused for a moment, then called out, "Hey, Eva! How about staying a little longer?"
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 <u>She</u>가 가리키는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: She = Ms. Blake. Eva에게 말을 건 사람.
det.analysis:
✅ ① Ms. Blake: 'called out'하며 Eva에게 제안. 주어 연결.
❌ ② Eva: Eva는 짐을 싸고 있는 중.
❌ ③ another player: 언급 없음.
❌ ④ the referee: 언급 없음.
det.tip: 대명사 She: 가장 가까운 여성 주어. Ms. Blake가 walked → paused → called out

questions.passage: After the game she ran over, saying, "Thanks for believing in me, Coach." Ms. Blake smiled back. "You've always had <u>it</u> in you. I'm just here to remind you of that."
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 <u>it</u>이 가리키는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: it = 재능과 잠재력(talent and potential).
det.analysis:
✅ ④ the talent and potential: 'have it in you' = 내면의 능력/재능.
❌ ① soccer ball: 물리적 물체가 아님.
❌ ② final game: 과거 사건이 아님.
❌ ③ team leadership: 부분적이지만 전체 능력을 의미.
det.tip: have it in you: it = 내면의 능력, 잠재력. 추상적 의미의 대명사
